criteria.label: Construction Type
criteria.method: IBC 2021 and 2025 BCNYS R-2 limits by stories, framing and podium.
criteria.confidenceReason: Wood framing with no podium, clear of the type's height and area limits.

criteria.label: Building Form
criteria.method: Double-loaded corridor wings 64 ft deep; past 300 ft of corridor the plate folds into an L, past 480 ft a U, past 720 ft a courtyard.
criteria.confidenceReason: There is no site plan yet, so the shape follows from the floor plate's length alone.

criteria.label: Electrical Service Size
criteria.method: NEC 220.84 optional multifamily calculation, one service per building.

inputs.name: Appliances per Unit
inputs.value: Range, dryer, water heater, 6 kW heat (NEC Annex D4(b))

criteria.confidenceReason: Amenity space and equipment are not measured, so the common area is priced at the clubs rate and pool or sauna equipment is left out. Elevator motors carry a 40 HP placeholder until the elevator vendor's data replaces it.

criteria.label: Window Area and Orientation
criteria.method: Glazing band from balconies and storefronts, mapped to DOE's apartment prototypes.
criteria.confidenceReason: No code or intake fact measures window area directly; balconies and storefronts point different ways, so the standard band is used.

criteria.label: HVAC Tonnage
criteria.method: Gross square feet over DOE's IECC 2021 apartment prototype GSF per ton, by climate zone and glazing band.

steps.label: Ventilation Check
steps.result: 53 cfm per 1,000 SF, within the model's 58

criteria.confidenceReason: New construction in a stated climate zone, with no garage in the area and ventilation within the model; the ratio is DOE's code-minimum model, not a load calculation for this building.

criteria.label: Foundation System
criteria.method: Bearing pressure over IBC Class 4's presumptive value, then ground and basement.

steps.label: Ground
steps.result: Not known, priced as good ground

criteria.confidenceReason: There is no geotechnical report yet. Ground conditions are not known, so ground improvement or deep foundations may still be needed. Rock is possible in this area, so footings and trenches may need rock excavation.

criteria.label: Elevator Type
criteria.method: Travel from Stories Above Grade against the hydraulic-to-traction band.

steps.label: Band
steps.result: Either; nothing set up to choose, so Hydraulic

criteria.confidenceReason: Travel of 40.0 ft sits inside the either band (over 35 ft, up to 55 ft), where hydraulic and traction are both common. Nothing is set up to choose between the two, so V-1 proposes Hydraulic, the cheaper type.

criteria.label: Hydraulic Jack Type
criteria.method: Travel against each jack's reach in the manufacturers' planning guides.

steps.label: Band
steps.result: Over 34 ft, up to 48 ft -> In-Ground

criteria.confidenceReason: Travel of 40.0 ft works either way, and nobody has said whether the ground is wet, so V-2 prices the well hole to be safe. This ZIP can hit shallow rock, and the intake does not ask about rock, so confidence is low.

criteria.label: Elevator Machine Rooms
criteria.method: Machine rooms by elevator type, count and building.

steps.label: Machine Rooms
steps.result: 1 (one per building, cars in one bank)

criteria.confidenceReason: Hydraulic cars share one machine room per bank at the lowest landing (Otis, Schindler), conditioned to the maker's range (IBC 3005.2). With 2 cars in a building, separate cores would double the rooms. V-1 could still flip to traction, which has no machine room.
